messages.author: 789ad20659f85e51
messages.subject: RSFs for different behaviors
parts:
Hi,

I'd like to look at habitat selection for my birds while theyre in 3 different states- nighttime roosting, daytime active, and daytime inactive. Is it better to build a separate ctmm fit and utilization distribution for each of these, or should i just build a single one from all the data,  and feed each set into the rsf fit individually?

Thanks!

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: RSFs for different behaviors
parts:
Hi Marian,

Active and inactive/roosting behaviors will be very different and will require different stationary models. The active data is the easiest to work with, because you can stick it all in to one model without modification, and it is usually what you want to analyze for the UD and RSF.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: RSFs for different behaviors
parts:
Hi Marian,

You can use ctmm, but regardless of what you use, you may have to work with the data to make it suitable for a single stationary model - and the IID models assumed by simpler methods are stationary.
The issue is that multiple fixes at during one inactive period are essentially pseudo-replicants, and one stationary model can't explain the displacement achieved between the inactive periods.

A simple solution is given here: https://groups.google.com/g/ctmm-user/c/g5UDb40gtUQ/m/2JyshES7BAAJ

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: RSFs for different behaviors
parts:
Hi Marian,

You will want to segment the active/inactive daytime movement. The active segments are the easiest to work with.

You could inflate the time intervals for both daytime and nighttime inactive data. Alternatively, if the inactive segments are reduced to one point per inactive period, then you could just fit an IID model to them.

Best,
Chris
